{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01CDU6zoUyFwh7WbBZezhzWr","type":"tool_result","content":"     1→# Netsmart Technologies — Product Research\n     2→\n     3→Researched: 2026-02-16\n     4→Developer website: https://www.ntst.com/\n     5→\n     6→## Overview\n     7→\n     8→Netsmart Technologies is a major healthcare IT company headquartered in Overland Park, Kansas, with technology origins dating back to 1968 (Creative Socio-Medics, acquired 1994). The company specializes in EHR and health information technology for **behavioral health, human services, and post-acute care** — a distinct market niche compared to the acute/ambulatory EHR giants like Epic and Oracle Health. Netsmart has undergone significant private equity ownership transitions: Genstar Capital acquired it in 2010, then GI Partners and Allscripts bought it for $950M in 2016 (Allscripts merged its homecare software business into Netsmart), and in 2018 GI Partners and TA Associates acquired Allscripts' stake. Netsmart remains privately held under GI Partners.\n     9→\n    10→The company reported $319M in revenue in 2018 and claims more than 23,000 customer organizations, 450,000+ care providers, and 40+ state systems as users. Its product portfolio is organized under the **CareFabric** platform and includes multiple EHR products: **myAvatar** (behavioral health), **myEvolv** (addiction/autism/IDD), **myUnity** (post-acute care), **GEHRIMED** (geriatric/LTC physician practices), and **TheraOffice** (physical therapy). Netsmart has made 17+ acquisitions, including HealthMEDX (LTC EHR, 2016), McBee (healthcare consulting, 2019), and Netalytics (addiction treatment, 2023). The company also provides AI tools (Bells AI for documentation, AlphaCoding for coding), interoperability/HIE services, workforce management, analytics, and revenue cycle management services across its platform.\n    11→\n    12→## Product: myUnity\n    13→\n    14→CHPL IDs: 11409\n    15→\n    16→### What It Is\n    17→\n    18→myUnity is Netsmart's **unified post-acute care EHR platform** — a single integrated system designed to serve the full spectrum of post-acute and senior care settings. Unlike many EHRs that target one care setting, myUnity explicitly spans:\n    19→\n    20→- **Home Health**\n    21→- **Hospice**\n    22→- **Palliative Care**\n    23→- **Skilled Nursing Facilities (SNF)**\n    24→- **Senior Living** (assisted living, independent living, memory care)\n    25→- **Life Plan Communities / CCRCs** (Continuing Care Retirement Communities)\n    26→- **Personal Care / Private Duty**\n    27→- **Adult Day Care**\n    28→- **State Veterans Homes**\n    29→\n    30→The certified module (CHPL #11409, version 2023) carries a broad set of ONC certifications covering clinical data (a)(1)-(a)(5), (a)(12), (a)(14); transitions of care (b)(1)-(b)(3); EHI export (b)(10)-(b)(11); clinical quality measures (c)(1)-(c)(3); patient portal/VDT (e)(1), (e)(3); public health reporting (f)(1), (f)(5); and FHIR API access (g)(7), (g)(9), (g)(10). There is also a separate \"myUnity Senior Living\" ONC certification mentioned on the certifications page. The product is cloud-based and part of the broader Netsmart CareFabric ecosystem.\n    31→\n    32→The next-generation version, **myUnity NX**, was demonstrated at LeadingAge 2024 and features redesigned UX, integrated AI, and enhanced mobile capabilities, described as \"designed by clinicians for clinicians.\"\n    33→\n    34→### Users & Market\n    35→\n    36→myUnity targets **post-acute care providers** across all care settings. Day-to-day users include:\n    37→\n    38→- **Home health nurses and clinicians** performing bedside documentation during visits\n    39→- **Hospice interdisciplinary teams** (physicians, nurses, social workers, chaplains, bereavement counselors)\n    40→- **Skilled nursing facility staff** handling MDS assessments and resident care\n    41→- **Senior living administrators and caregivers** managing residents across assisted living, memory care, and independent living\n    42→- **Billing and administrative staff** across all settings\n    43→- **Practice managers and compliance officers**\n    44→\n    45→Notable deployments include:\n    46→- **Interim HealthCare** agencies implementing myUnity as their EHR platform (Yahoo Finance press coverage)\n    47→- **Ohio's Hospice** implementing Netsmart EHR system across their network\n    48→- The product has **CHAP Verification** for both home health and hospice, a quality accreditation\n    49→\n    50→Netsmart claims significant market share in post-acute care, receiving 28 Black Book Research awards in 2025, including #1 rankings in behavioral health, long-term care, and value-based care technology. However, KLAS research presents a more mixed picture — about two-thirds of surveyed customers said they would not buy their Netsmart solution again, citing concerns about development pace and support relative to sales emphasis.\n    51→\n    52→### Modules & Functionality\n    53→\n    54→myUnity is organized around care-setting-specific workflows within a single integrated platform. Key modules and capabilities found in vendor materials:\n    55→\n    56→**Home Health Module:**\n    57→- Point-of-care clinical documentation on mobile devices during visits\n    58→- OASIS-E assessment compliance and completion tools\n    59→- PDGM (Patient-Driven Groupings Model) billing support\n    60→- Electronic Visit Verification (EVV) via Mobile Caregiver+\n    61→- CareRouter mobile dispatch for staff triaging and urgent visit scheduling\n    62→- Orders management with physician signature workflows\n    63→- Medication management with batch updates and reconciliation\n    64→- Care plan creation and management\n    65→- Interoperability via Carequality and HIE connections to import CCDAs, allergies, medications, diagnoses\n    66→\n    67→**Hospice Module:**\n    68→- Interdisciplinary Group (IDG) meeting workflows with automated agenda development\n    69→- Bereavement care plan creation, management, and tracking\n    70→- Inpatient Unit (IPU) management including patient status, interim care, and continuous care tracking\n    71→- HOPE assessment scrubbing (compliance tool)\n    72→- Physician orders management\n    73→- Medication tracking including dosage and administration schedules\n    74→- Symptom management documentation\n    75→- Care coordination across interdisciplinary teams\n    76→\n    77→**Skilled Nursing Module:**\n    78→- MDS (Minimum Data Set) assessment tools\n    79→- PDPM (Patient-Driven Payment Model) optimization via Netsmart Simple analytics\n    80→- Near real-time predictive MDS analytics (CORE Analytics)\n    81→- Single resident record spanning all care levels within a community\n    87→- Care planning with personalized activity scheduling\n    88→- Health monitoring with real-time metrics and alert systems\n    89→- Medication management and eMAR\n    90→- Incident reporting\n    91→- Role-based customizable views\n    92→- Billing across care levels with unified patient statements\n    93→\n API data (certified for (g)(7), (g)(9), (g)(10))\n   158→- Transitions of care documents\n   159→\n   160→The vendor website does not explicitly discuss some data types that might be present in such a This value\ncannot be updated by a myUnity user.\n\nPatientID\n\nPatientID is the typical method to indicate the unique patient\nidentifier within the myUnity environment. This is sometimes\nreferred to as the medical record number or client ID. This value\nshould be used to associate all files to a specific patient.\nConcatenation of the patient’s Last, First and Middle portions of\ntheir legal name.\n\nPatient_DisplayName\n\n3\n\n\fDemographics File Documentation\nFile Description: This file contains basic demographic details for the\npatient.\n-------------Name: PatientSys\nType: Integer\nDescription: Unique identifier of the patient\nName: PatientID\nType: String\nDescription: myUnity internal identifier. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_013h8znE2pNn4z3j18pBi6v6","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01F5wm58geSZyhaTkQXbnixf","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"# Extract the core content section\npython3 -c \"\nimport re\nwith open('/tmp/ntst-ehi-myunity.html', 'r') as f:\n    html = f.read()\n# Find 'EHI Export' related content\n# Look for the section that starts with the EHI description\nmatch = re.search(r'EHI Export functionality allows.*?</div>', html, re.DOTALL)\nif match:\n    section = match.group()\n    # Strip tags\n    text = re.sub(r'<[^>]+>', ' ', section)\n    text = re.sub(r'\\s+', ' ', text).strip()\n    print(text[:3000])\nelse:\n    print('No match for EHI Export functionality')\n    # Try broader search\n    match = re.search(r'EHI \\(Electronic Health Information\\) All Data Export for myUnity.*?(?=<footer|<!-- Footer)', html, re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE)\n    if match:\n        section = match.group()\n        text = re.sub(r'<script[^>]*>.*?</script>', ' ', section, flags=re.DOTALL)\n        text = re.sub(r'<style[^>]*>.*?</style>', ' ', section, flags=re.DOTALL)\n        text = re.sub(r'<[^>]+>', ' ', text)\n        text = re.sub(r'\\s+', ' ', text).strip()\n        print(text[:3000])\n\"\n","description":"Extract EHI export description from HTML"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1512,"cache_read_input_tokens":59117,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1512},"output_tokens":7,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"db0d5107-7ffe-4c49-89d2-6ef77b08d733","uuid":"8bfcc98f-922f-431b-9877-1af2a1423ce1"}

The documentation\nreflects the most current information at the time it was produced. The\ndocumentation is broken out by export file. Documentation from a\nspecific organization might differ based on the organization's version of\nmyUnity, custom development, or definition of EHI data. Each file\ncontains a description and column details.\n\nGlossary of Terms\nIn order to assist organizations in interpreting the information here,\nNetsmart is providing a glossary of terms for those commonly used field\ndescriptions.\nField Name\n\nDescription\n\nPatientSys\n\nThe unique system generated ID for a given patient. This value\ncannot be updated by a myUnity user.\n\nPatientID\n\nPatientID is the typical method to indicate the unique patient\nidentifier within the myUnity environment. This is sometimes\nreferred to as the medical record number or client ID. This value\nshould be used to associate all files to a specific patient.\nConcatenation of the patient’s Last, First and Middle portions of\ntheir legal name.\n\nPatient_DisplayName\n\n3\n\n\fDemographics File Documentation\nFile Description: This file contains basic demographic details for the\npatient.\n-------------Name: PatientSys\nType: Integer\nDescription: Unique identifier of the patient\nName: PatientID\nType: String\nDescription: myUnity internal identifier. while (i < lines.length) {\n          const contLine = lines[i].trim();\n          if (\n            separatorPattern.test(contLine) ||\n            contLine.startsWith(\"Name:\") ||\n            contLine.startsWith(\"CCD contains\")\n          ) {\n            break;\n          }\n          if (contLine && !pageNumberPattern.test(contLine)) {\n            fileDescription += \" \" + contLine;\n          }\n          i++;\n        }\n        foundDesc = true;\n        break;\n      }\n      if (separatorPattern.test(nextLine) || nextLine.startsWith(\"Name:\")) {\n        break;\n      }\n      i++;\n    }\n\n    // Special case for CCD file — it has sections, not fields\n    if (fileName === \"CCD\") {\n      const sections: string[] = [];\n      while (i < lines.length) {\n        const sLine = lines[i].trim();\n        if (sLine.match(fileDocPattern) && sLine !== line) break;\n        if (sLine.startsWith(\"•\")) {\n          sections.push(sLine.replace(\"•\", \"\").trim());\n        }\n        i++;\n      }\n      exportFiles.push({\n        file_name: fileName,\n        file_description: fileDescription,\n        fields: [],\n        sections,\n      });\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    // Special case for Attachments — no fields, just description\n    if (fileName === \"Attachments\") {\n      exportFiles.push({\n        file_name: fileName,\n        file_description: fileDescription,\n        fields: [],\n      });\n      // Don't increment i, let the outer loop handle it\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    // Parse fields\n    const fields: Field[] }\n\n      // Skip page numbers and separators\n      if (pageNumberPattern.test(fLine) || separatorPattern.test(fLine) || fLine === \"\") {\n        i++;\n        continue;\n      }\n\n      const input_file: \"ehi_export_all_files_myunity_fall_2024.pdf\",\n  extraction_method: \"pdftotext + regex parsing\",\n  total_lines_processed: lines.length,\n  files_discovered: exportFiles.map((f) => fileMatch[1].trim();","originalFile":"#!/usr/bin/env bun\n/**\n * Extracts the myUnity EHI Export data dictionary from the PDF text extraction\n * into a structured JSON format.\n *\n * Input: pdftotext output of ehi_export_all_files_myunity_fall_2024.pdf\n * Output: data-dictionary.json — structured JSON with all files and fields\n */\n\nimport { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from \"fs\";\nimport { execSync } from \"child_process\";\nimport { join, dirname } from \"path\";\n\nconst scriptDir = dirname(new URL(import.meta.url).pathname);\nconst pdfPath = join(scriptDir, \"..\", \"ehi_export_all_files_myunity_fall_2024.pdf\");\n\n// Extract text from PDF\nconst text = execSync(`pdftotext \"${pdfPath}\" -`, { encoding: \"utf-8\" });\n\ninterface Field {\n  name: string;\n  type: string;\n  description: string;\n}\n\ninterface ExportFile {\n  file_name: string;\n  file_description: string;\n  fields: Field[];\n  sections?: string[]; // For CCD-like files that list sections instead of fields\n}\n\ninterface DataDictionary {\n  document_title: string;\n  last_updated: string;\n  overview: string;\n  glossary: Record<string, string>;\n  export_files: ExportFile[];\n  stats: {\n    total_files: number;\n    total_fields: number;\n    files_with_fields: number;\n    files_with_sections_only: number;\n  };\n}\n\n// Parse the text\nconst lines = text.split(\"\\n\");\n\n// Extract metadata\nconst title = \"EHI Export: myUnity File Documentation\";\nconst lastUpdated = \"08/15/2024 12:00 PM EDT\";\nconst overview =\n  \"This documentation describes each myUnity EHI file as of 03/01/2024 at 12:00 PM EDT in the current released version. The documentation reflects the most current information at the time it was produced. The documentation is broken out by export file. Documentation from a specific organization might differ based on the organization's version of myUnity, custom development, or definition of EHI data. Each file contains a description and column details.\";\n\n// Parse glossary\nconst glossary: Record<string, string> = {\n  PatientSys:\n    \"The unique system generated ID for a given patient. This value cannot be updated by a myUnity user.\",\n  PatientID:\n    \"PatientID is the typical method to indicate the unique patient identifier within the myUnity environment. This is sometimes referred to as the medical record number or client ID. This value should be used to associate all files to a specific patient.\",\n  Patient_DisplayName:\n    \"Concatenation of the patient's Last, First and Middle portions of their legal name.\",\n};\n\n// Find file documentation sections\n// Pattern: \"XXX File Documentation\"\nconst fileDocPattern = /^(.+?)\\s+File Documentation$/;\nconst fileDescPattern = /^File Description:\\s*(.+)/;\nconst fieldNamePattern = /^Name:\\s*(.+)/;\nconst fieldTypePattern = /^Type:\\s*(.+)/;\nconst fieldDescPattern = /^Description:\\s*(.+)/;\nconst pageNumberPattern = /^\\d+$/;\nconst separatorPattern = /^-{5,}/;\n\nconst exportFiles: ExportFile[] = [];\n\nlet i = 0;\nwhile (i < lines.length) {\n  const line = lines[i].trim();\n\n  // Check for file documentation header\n  const fileMatch = line.match(fileDocPattern);\n  if (fileMatch && !line.startsWith(\"Contents\") && !line.startsWith(\"Overview\")) {\n    const fileName = fileMatch[1].trim();\n\n    // Skip forward to find file description\n    i++;\n    let fileDescription = \"\";\n    let foundDesc = false;\n\n    // Collect file description (may span multiple lines)\n    while (i < lines.length) {\n      const nextLine = lines[i].trim();\n      if (pageNumberPattern.test(nextLine) || nextLine === \"\") {\n        i++;\n        continue;\n      }\n\n      if (nextLine.startsWith(\"File Description:\")) {\n        fileDescription = nextLine.replace(\"File Description:\", \"\").trim();\n        i++;\n        // Continue collecting description until we hit separator or field\n        while (i < lines.length) {\n          const contLine = lines[i].trim();\n          if (\n            separatorPattern.test(contLine) ||\n            contLine.startsWith(\"Name:\") ||\n            contLine.startsWith(\"CCD contains\")\n          ) {\n            break;\n          }\n          if (contLine && !pageNumberPattern.test(contLine)) {\n            fileDescription += \" \" + contLine;\n          }\n          i++;\n        }\n        foundDesc = true;\n        break;\n      }\n      if (separatorPattern.test(nextLine) || nextLine.startsWith(\"Name:\")) {\n        break;\n      }\n      i++;\n    }\n\n    // Special case for CCD file — it has sections, not fields\n    if (fileName === \"CCD\") {\n      const sections: string[] = [];\n      while (i < lines.length) {\n        const sLine = lines[i].trim();\n        if (sLine.match(fileDocPattern) && sLine !== line) break;\n        if (sLine.startsWith(\"•\")) {\n          sections.push(sLine.replace(\"•\", \"\").trim());\n        }\n        i++;\n      }\n      exportFiles.push({\n        file_name: fileName,\n        file_description: fileDescription,\n        fields: [],\n        sections,\n      });\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    // Special case for Attachments — no fields, just description\n    if (fileName === \"Attachments\") {\n      exportFiles.push({\n        file_name: fileName,\n        file_description: fileDescription,\n        fields: [],\n      });\n      // Don't increment i, let the outer loop handle it\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    // Parse fields\n    const fields: Field[] = [];\n    let currentName = \"\";\n    let currentType = \"\";\n    let currentDesc = \"\";\n    let collectingDesc = false;\n\n    while (i < lines.length) {\n      const fLine = lines[i].trim();\n\n      // Check if we've hit the next file documentation section\n      if (fLine.match(fileDocPattern) && fLine !== line) {\n        // Save any pending field\n        if (currentName) {\n          fields.push({\n            name: currentName,\n            type: currentType,\n            description: currentDesc.trim(),\n          });\n        }\n        break;\n      }\n\n      // Skip page numbers and separators\n      if (pageNumberPattern.test(fLine) || separatorPattern.test(fLine) || fLine === \"\") {\n        i++;\n        continue;\n      }\n\n      const nameMatch = fLine.match(fieldNamePattern);\n      const typeMatch = fLine.match(fieldTypePattern);\n      const descMatch = fLine.match(fieldDescPattern);\n\n      if (nameMatch) {\n        // Save previous field\n        if (currentName) {\n          fields.push({\n            name: currentName,\n            type: currentType,\n            description: currentDesc.trim(),\n          });\n        }\n        currentName = nameMatch[1].trim();\n        currentType = \"\";\n        currentDesc = \"\";\n        collectingDesc = false;\n      } else if (typeMatch && currentName && !currentType) {\n        currentType = typeMatch[1].trim();\n      } else if (descMatch && currentName && currentType) {\n        currentDesc = descMatch[1].trim();\n        collectingDesc = true;\n      } else if (collectingDesc && fLine && !fLine.startsWith(\"Name:\") && !fLine.startsWith(\"Type:\")) {\n        // Multi-line description continuation\n        currentDesc += \" \" + fLine;\n      } else if (!currentName && !nameMatch && !typeMatch && !descMatch) {\n        // Could be continuation of file description or other text\n        i++;\n        continue;\n      }\n\n      i++;\n    }\n\n    // Save last field if we ran out of lines\n    if (currentName) {\n      fields.push({\n        name: currentName,\n        type: currentType,\n        description: currentDesc.trim(),\n      });\n    }\n\n    exportFiles.push({\n      file_name: fileName,\n      file_description: fileDescription,\n      fields,\n    });\n    continue;\n  }\n\n  i++;\n}\n\n// Compute stats\nconst totalFields = exportFiles.reduce((sum, f) => sum + f.fields.length, 0);\nconst filesWithFields = exportFiles.filter((f) => f.fields.length > 0).length;\nconst filesWithSectionsOnly = exportFiles.filter(\n  (f) => f.fields.length === 0 && f.sections && f.sections.length > 0\n).length;\n\nconst dictionary: DataDictionary = {\n  document_title: title,\n  last_updated: lastUpdated,\n  overview,\n  glossary,\n  export_files: exportFiles,\n  stats: {\n    total_files: exportFiles.length,\n    total_fields: totalFields,\n    files_with_fields: filesWithFields,\n    files_with_sections_only: filesWithSectionsOnly,\n  },\n};\n\nconst outputPath = join(scriptDir, \"data-dictionary.json\");\nwriteFileSync(outputPath, JSON.stringify(dictionary, null, 2));\n\n// Print summary\nconsole.log(`Parsed ${exportFiles.length} export files`);\nconsole.log(`Total fields extracted: ${totalFields}`);\nconsole.log(`Files with field definitions: // For CCD-like files that list sections instead of fields\n}\n\ninterface DataDictionary {\n  document_title: string;\n  last_updated: string;\n  overview: string;\n  glossary: Record<string, string>;\n  export_files: ExportFile[];\n  stats: {\n    total_files: number;\n    total_fields: number;\n    files_with_fields: number;\n    files_with_sections_only: number;\n  };\n}\n\n// Parse the text\nconst lines = text.split(\"\\n\");\n\n// Extract metadata\nconst title = \"EHI Export: myUnity File Documentation\";\nconst lastUpdated = \"08/15/2024 12:00 PM EDT\";\nconst overview =\n  \"This documentation describes each myUnity EHI file as of 03/01/2024 at 12:00 PM EDT in the current released version. The documentation reflects the most current information at the time it was produced. The documentation is broken out by export file. Documentation from a specific organization might differ based on the organization's version of myUnity, custom development, or definition of EHI data. Each file contains a description and column details.\";\n\n// Parse glossary\nconst glossary: Record<string, string> = {\n  PatientSys:\n    \"The unique system generated ID for a given patient. This value cannot be updated by a myUnity user.\",\n  PatientID:\n    \"PatientID is the typical method to indicate the unique patient identifier within the myUnity environment. This is sometimes referred to as the medical record number or client ID. This value should be used to associate all files to a specific patient.\",\n  Patient_DisplayName:\n    \"Concatenation of the patient's Last, First and Middle portions of their legal name.\",\n};\n\n// Find file documentation sections\n// Pattern: \"XXX File Documentation\"\nconst fileDocPattern = /^(.+?)\\s+File Documentation$/;\nconst fileDescPattern = /^File Description:\\s*(.+)/;\nconst fieldNamePattern = /^Name:\\s*(.+)/;\nconst fieldTypePattern = /^Type:\\s*(.+)/;\nconst fieldDescPattern = /^Description:\\s*(.+)/;\nconst pageNumberPattern = /^\\d+$/;\nconst separatorPattern = /^-{5,}/;\n\nconst exportFiles: ExportFile[] = [];\n\nlet i = 0;\nwhile (i < lines.length) {\n  const line = lines[i].trim();\n\n  // Check for file documentation header\n  const fileMatch = line.match(fileDocPattern);\n  if (\n    fileMatch &&\n    !line.startsWith(\"Contents\") &&\n    !line.startsWith(\"Overview\") &&\n    !line.startsWith(\"EHI Export:\") &&\n    !line.includes(\"....\") // Skip TOC lines\n  ) {\n    const fileName = fileMatch[1].trim();\n\n    // Skip forward to find file description\n    i++;\n    let fileDescription = \"\";\n    let foundDesc = false;\n\n    // Collect file description (may span multiple lines)\n    while (i < lines.length) {\n      const nextLine = lines[i].trim();\n      if (pageNumberPattern.test(nextLine) || writeFileSync } from \"fs\";\nimport { execSync } from \"child_process\";\nimport { join, dirname } from \"path\";\n\nconst scriptDir = dirname(new URL(import.meta.url).pathname);\nconst pdfPath = {\n  name: string;\n  type: string;\n  description: string;\n}\n\ninterface ExportFile {\n  file_name: string;\n  file_description: string;\n  fields: Field[];\n  sections?: string[]; // For CCD-like files that list sections instead of fields\n}\n\ninterface DataDictionary {\n  document_title: string;\n  last_updated: string;\n  overview: string;\n  glossary: Record<string, string>;\n  export_files: ExportFile[];\n  stats: {\n    total_files: number;\n    total_fields: number;\n    files_with_fields: number;\n    files_with_sections_only: number;\n  };\n}\n\n// Parse the text\nconst lines = text.split(\"\\n\");\n\n// Extract metadata\nconst title = \"EHI Export: myUnity File Documentation\";\nconst lastUpdated = \"08/15/2024 12:00 PM EDT\";\nconst overview =\n  \"This documentation describes each myUnity EHI file as of 03/01/2024 at 12:00 PM EDT in the current released version. The documentation reflects the most current information at the time it was produced. The documentation is broken out by export file. Documentation from a specific organization might differ based on the organization's version of myUnity, custom development, or definition of EHI data. Each file contains a description and column details.\";\n\n// Parse glossary\nconst glossary: Record<string, string> = {\n  PatientSys:\n    \"The unique system generated ID for a given patient. This value cannot be updated by a myUnity user.\",\n  PatientID:\n    \"PatientID is the typical method to indicate the unique patient identifier within the myUnity environment. This is sometimes referred to as the medical record number or client ID. This value should be used to associate all files to a specific patient.\",\n  Patient_DisplayName:\n    \"Concatenation of the patient's Last, First and Middle portions of their legal name.\",\n};\n\n// Find file documentation sections\n// Pattern: \"XXX File Documentation\"\nconst fileDocPattern = /^(.+?)\\s+File Documentation$/;\nconst fileDescPattern = /^File Description:\\s*(.+)/;\nconst fieldNamePattern = /^Name:\\s*(.+)/;\nconst fieldTypePattern = /^Type:\\s*(.+)/;\nconst fieldDescPattern = /^Description:\\s*(.+)/;\nconst pageNumberPattern = /^\\d+$/;\nconst separatorPattern = /^-{5,}/;\n// Handle merged separator+name lines like \"-------------Name: PatientSys\"\nconst mergedSepNamePattern = /^-{5,}Name:\\s*(.+)/;\n\nconst exportFiles: ExportFile[] = [];\n\nlet i = 0;\nwhile (i < lines.length) {\n  const line = lines[i].trim();\n\n  // Check for file documentation header\n  const fileMatch = line.match(fileDocPattern);\n  if (\n    fileMatch &&\n    !line.startsWith(\"Contents\") &&\n    !line.startsWith(\"Overview\") &&\n    !line.startsWith(\"EHI Export:\") &&\n    !line.includes(\"....\") // Skip TOC lines\n  ) {\n    const fileName = fileMatch[1].trim();\n\n    // Skip forward to find file description\n    i++;\n    let fileDescription = \"\";\n    let foundDesc = false;\n\n    // Collect file description (may span multiple lines)\n    while (i < lines.length) {\n      const nextLine = lines[i].trim();\n      if (pageNumberPattern.test(nextLine) || nextLine === \"\") {\n        i++;\n        continue;\n continue;","originalFile":"#!/usr/bin/env bun\n/**\n * Extracts the myUnity EHI Export data dictionary from the PDF text extraction\n * into a structured JSON format.\n *\n * Input: pdftotext output execSync } from \"child_process\";\nimport { join, dirname } from \"path\";\n\nconst scriptDir = dirname(new URL(import.meta.url).pathname);\nconst pdfPath = join(scriptDir, \"..\", \"ehi_export_all_files_myunity_fall_2024.pdf\");\n\n// Extract text from PDF\nconst text = execSync(`pdftotext \"${pdfPath}\" -`, { encoding: \"utf-8\" });\n\ninterface Field {\n  name: string;\n  type: string;\n  description: string;\n}\n\ninterface ExportFile {\n  file_name: string;\n  file_description: string;\n  fields: Field[];\n  sections?: string[]; // For CCD-like files that list sections instead of fields\n}\n\ninterface DataDictionary {\n  document_title: string;\n  last_updated: string;\n  overview: string;\n  glossary: Record<string, string>;\n  export_files: ExportFile[];\n  stats: {\n    total_files: number;\n    total_fields: number;\n    files_with_fields: number;\n    files_with_sections_only: number;\n  };\n}\n\n// Parse the text\nconst lines = text.split(\"\\n\");\n\n// Extract metadata\nconst title = \"EHI Export: myUnity File Documentation\";\nconst lastUpdated = \"08/15/2024 12:00 PM EDT\";\nconst overview =\n  \"This documentation describes each myUnity EHI file as of 03/01/2024 at 12:00 PM EDT in the current released version. The documentation reflects the most current information at the time it was produced. The documentation is broken out by export file. Documentation from a specific organization might differ based on the organization's version of myUnity, custom development, or definition of EHI data. Each file contains a description and column details.\";\n\n// Parse glossary\nconst glossary: Record<string, string> = {\n  PatientSys:\n    \"The unique system generated ID for a given patient. This value cannot be updated by a myUnity user.\",\n  PatientID:\n    \"PatientID is the typical method to indicate the unique patient identifier within the myUnity environment. This is sometimes referred to as the medical record number or client ID. This value should be used to associate all files to a specific patient.\",\n  Patient_DisplayName:\n    \"Concatenation of the patient's Last, First and Middle portions of their legal name.\",\n};\n\n// Find file documentation sections\n// Pattern: \"XXX File Documentation\"\nconst fileDocPattern = /^(.+?)\\s+File Documentation$/;\nconst fileDescPattern = /^File Description:\\s*(.+)/;\nconst fieldNamePattern = /^Name:\\s*(.+)/;\nconst fieldTypePattern = /^Type:\\s*(.+)/;\nconst fieldDescPattern = /^Description:\\s*(.+)/;\nconst pageNumberPattern = /^\\d+$/;\nconst separatorPattern = /^-{5,}/;\n// Handle merged separator+name lines like \"-------------Name: PatientSys\"\nconst mergedSepNamePattern = /^-{5,}Name:\\s*(.+)/;\n\nconst exportFiles: ExportFile[] = [];\n\nlet i = 0;\nwhile (i < lines.length) {\n  const line = lines[i].trim();\n\n  // Check for file documentation header\n  const fileMatch = line.match(fileDocPattern);\n  if (\n    fileMatch &&\n    !line.startsWith(\"Contents\") &&\n    !line.startsWith(\"Overview\") &&\n    !line.startsWith(\"EHI Export:\") &&\n    !line.includes(\"....\") // Skip TOC lines\n  ) {\n    const fileName = fileMatch[1].trim();\n\n    // Skip forward to find file description\n    i++;\n    let fileDescription = \"\";\n    let foundDesc = false;\n\n    // Collect file description (may span multiple lines)\n    while (i < lines.length) {\n      const nextLine = lines[i].trim();\n      if (pageNumberPattern.test(nextLine) || nextLine === \"\") {\n        i++;\n        continue;\n      }\n\n      if (nextLine.startsWith(\"File Description:\")) {\n        fileDescription = nextLine.replace(\"File Description:\", \"\").trim();\n        i++;\n        // Continue collecting description until we hit separator or field\n        while (i < lines.length) {\n          const contLine = lines[i].trim();\n          if (\n            separatorPattern.test(contLine) ||\n            mergedSepNamePattern.test(contLine) ||\n            contLine.startsWith(\"Name:\") ||\n            contLine.startsWith(\"CCD contains\")\n          ) {\n            break;\n          }\n          if (contLine && !pageNumberPattern.test(contLine)) {\n            fileDescription += \" \" + contLine;\n          }\n          i++;\n        }\n        foundDesc = true;\n        break;\n      }\n      if (separatorPattern.test(nextLine) || nextLine.startsWith(\"Name:\")) {\n        break;\n      }\n      i++;\n    }\n\n    // Special case for CCD file — it has sections, not fields\n    if (fileName === \"CCD\") {\n      const sections: string[] = [];\n      while (i < lines.length) {\n        const sLine = lines[i].trim();\n        if (sLine.match(fileDocPattern) && sLine !== line) break;\n        if (sLine.startsWith(\"•\")) {\n          sections.push(sLine.replace(\"•\", \"\").trim());\n        }\n        i++;\n      }\n      exportFiles.push({\n        file_name: fileName,\n        file_description: fileDescription,\n        fields: [],\n        sections,\n      });\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    // Special case for Attachments — no fields, just description\n    if (fileName === \"Attachments\") {\n      exportFiles.push({\n        file_name: fileName,\n        file_description: fileDescription,\n        fields: [],\n      });\n      // Don't increment i, let the outer loop handle it\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    // Parse fields\n    const fields: Field[] = [];\n    let currentName = \"\";\n    let currentType = \"\";\n    let currentDesc = \"\";\n    let collectingDesc = false;\n\n    while (i < lines.length) {\n      const fLine = lines[i].trim();\n\n      // Check if we've hit the next file documentation section\n      if (fLine.match(fileDocPattern) && fLine !== line) {\n        // Save any pending field\n        if (currentName) {\n          fields.push({\n            name: currentName,\n            type: currentType,\n            description: currentDesc.trim(),\n          });\n        }\n        break;\n      }\n\n      // Skip page numbers and plain separators\n      if (pageNumberPattern.test(fLine) || fLine === \"\") {\n        i++;\n        continue;\n      }\n\n      // Handle merged separator+name like \"-------------Name: PatientSys\"\n      const mergedMatch = fLine.match(mergedSepNamePattern);\n      if (mergedMatch) {\n        if (currentName) {\n          fields.push({\n            name: currentName,\n            type: currentType,\n            description: currentDesc.trim(),\n          });\n        }\n        currentName = mergedMatch[1].trim();\n        currentType = \"\";\n        currentDesc = \"\";\n        collectingDesc = false;\n        i++;\n        continue;\n      }\n\n      // Skip plain separators (no merged content)\n      if (separatorPattern.test(fLine)) {\n        i++;\n        continue;\n      }\n\n      const nameMatch = fLine.match(fieldNamePattern);\n      const typeMatch = fLine.match(fieldTypePattern);\n      const descMatch = fLine.match(fieldDescPattern);\n\n      if (nameMatch) {\n        // Save previous field\n        if (currentName) {\n          fields.push({\n            name: currentName,\n            type: currentType,\n            description: currentDesc.trim(),\n          });\n        }\n        currentName = nameMatch[1].trim();\n        currentType = \"\";\n        currentDesc = \"\";\n        collectingDesc = false;\n      } else if (typeMatch && currentName && !currentType) {\n        currentType = typeMatch[1].trim();\n      } else if (descMatch && currentName && currentType) {\n        currentDesc = descMatch[1].trim();\n        collectingDesc = true;\n      } else if (collectingDesc && fLine && !fLine.startsWith(\"Name:\") && !fLine.startsWith(\"Type:\")) {\n        // Multi-line description continuation\n        currentDesc += \" \" + fLine;\n      } else if (!currentName && !nameMatch && !typeMatch && !descMatch) {\n        // Could be continuation of file description or other text\n        i++;\n        continue;\n      }\n\n      i++;\n    }\n\n    // Save last field if we ran out of lines\n    if (currentName) {\n      fields.push({\n        name: currentName,\n        type: currentType,\n        description: currentDesc.trim(),\n      });\n    }\n\n    exportFiles.push({\n      file_name: fileName,\n      file_description: fileDescription,\n      fields,\n    });\n    continue;\n  }\n\n  i++;\n}\n\n// Compute stats\nconst totalFields = exportFiles.reduce((sum, f) => sum + f.fields.length, 0);\nconst filesWithFields = exportFiles.filter((f) => f.fields.length > 0).length;\nconst filesWithSectionsOnly = exportFiles.filter(\n  (f) => f.fields.length === 0 && f.sections && f.sections.length > 0\n).length;\n\nconst dictionary: DataDictionary = {\n  document_title: title,\n  last_updated: lastUpdated,\n  overview,\n  glossary,\n  export_files: exportFiles,\n  stats: {\n    total_files: exportFiles.length,\n    total_fields: totalFields,\n    files_with_fields: filesWithFields,\n    files_with_sections_only: filesWithSectionsOnly,\n  },\n};\n\nconst outputPath = join(scriptDir, \"data-dictionary.json\");\nwriteFileSync(outputPath, JSON.stringify(dictionary, null, 2));\n\n// Print summary\nconsole.log(`Parsed ${exportFiles.length} export files`);\nconsole.log(`Total fields files:`);\nfor (const f of exportFiles) {\n  const detail = f.sections\n    ? `${f.sections.length} sections`\n    : `${f.fields.length} fields`;\n  console.log(`  - ${f.file_name}: ${detail}`);\n}\n\n// Also produce a coverage accounting file\nconst accounting = {\n  input_file: \"ehi_export_all_files_myunity_fall_2024.pdf\",\n  extraction_method: \"pdftotext + regex  \"The NonRegulatoryAssessment file uses nested arrays (AssessmentDocList, Responses) with dot-notation field names\",\n    \"Field descriptions may span multiple lines in the PDF; parser concatenates {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_01KaLeSHe5rCvgFXCXosZPXY","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_013Qpvn7KepQQsjoTYE13CpS","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/netsmart-technologies--myunity/downloads/enrichment/README.md","content":"# myUnity EHI Export Data Dictionary Enrichment\n\n## Run Command\n\n```bash\nbun run extract-data-dictionary.ts\n```\n\n## Input\n\n- `../ehi_export_all_files_myunity_fall_2024.pdf` — 64-page PDF data dictionary\n- Text extraction via `pdftotext` (poppler-utils)\n\n## Output Files\n\n- `data-dictionary.json` — Structured JSON with all 23 export files and their field definitions (404 fields total)\n- `coverage-accounting.json` — Extraction statistics and notes\n\n## Known Parsing Limitations\n\n- `pdftotext` sometimes merges separator lines with the first field name (e.g., `-------------Name: PatientSys`); the parser handles this explicitly\n- Multi-line field descriptions are concatenated; line breaks within descriptions may not be perfectly preserved\n- The CCD file lists C-CDA sections rather than individual fields (it exports an XML CCD document)\n- The Attachments file has no field definitions — it exports raw files (pdf, doc, jpg, etc.)\n- Page numbers embedded in the text are filtered out but occasionally may be adjacent to content\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":512,"cache_read_input_tokens":100137,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":512},"output_tokens":1,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"db0d5107-7ffe-4c49-89d2-6ef77b08d733","uuid":"d997dcfc-94c8-4ccb-ad8d-8c446b74bb2a"}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_01RL4atG6GvmywNvPpLfHYXZ","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01Cp9wBdLdGizsiN3CFAimZc","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/netsmart-technologies--myunity/ehi-export-report.md","content":"# Netsmart Technologies — myUnity EHI Export Documentation\n\nCollected: 2026-02-16\n\n## Source\n- Registered URL: https://www.ntst.com/lp/certifications\n- CHPL IDs: 11409\n- Product: myUnity (version 2023)\n- Certification date: 2023-12-18\n\n## Navigation Journal\n\n1. **Probed the registered URL** with `curl -sI -L https://www.ntst.com/lp/certifications` — returned HTTP 200, Content-Type text/html, 189KB page. This is Netsmart's main certifications hub for all products.\n\n2. **Fetched and searched the page** for EHI-related links:\n   ```bash\n   curl -sL \"https://www.ntst.com/lp/certifications\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o /tmp/ntst-certifications.html\n   grep -oiE 'href=\"[^\"]*\"' /tmp/ntst-certifications.html | grep -iE 'ehi|export|myunity'\n   ```\n   Found product-specific EHI pages including `/lp/certifications/ehi-all-data-myunity`.\n\n3. **Navigated to the myUnity EHI page**: `https://www.ntst.com/lp/certifications/ehi-all-data-myunity`\n   - Page title: \"EHI (Electronic Health Information) All Data Export\"\n   - Subheading: \"EHI (Electronic Health Information) All Data Export for myUnity® and myUnity® Senior Living\"\n   - Page describes the export as a \"manual one-time export of health data for one or more patients\" in \"computable, JSON file format native to myUnity\"\n   - Single \"CLICK HERE\" link to the PDF data dictionary\n\n4. **Downloaded the PDF data dictionary**:\n   ```bash\n   curl -sL \"https://www.ntst.com/-/media/pdfs/certifications/ehi_export_all_files_myunity_fall_2024.pdf\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o ehi_export_all_files_myunity_fall_2024.pdf\n   ```\n   Verified: `file` reports \"PDF document, version 1.7, 64 page(s)\", 467KB. Created by Microsoft Word, dated 2024-08-26.\n\n5. **Examined the PDF** with `pdftotext` — clean text extraction. Full data dictionary with field-level documentation for 23 export files.\n\n6. **Checked for additional links** on the EHI page. Found two non-EHI links:\n   - Netsmart Developer Portal (https://careconnect-uat.netsmartcloud.com/) — for FHIR API integration, separate from EHI export\n   - Information Sharing page (https://www.ntst.com/lp/information-sharing) — general integration contact info\n   Neither contains additional EHI export documentation.\n\n7. **Checked the mandatory disclosures PDF** (`myunity-certification-status-letter_mandatory-costs-disclosures_01-02-2025.pdf`) — lists (b)(10) EHI Export as an included capability at no additional cost, but contains no technical documentation.\n\n8. **Ran enrichment** — parsed the PDF into structured JSON with `bun run extract-data-dictionary.ts`, producing `data-dictionary.json` with all 23 files and 404 fields.\n\n## What Was Found\n\n### Export Format\n\nThe myUnity EHI export produces **JSON files inside a ZIP archive**, one ZIP per patient. This is a proprietary, vendor-native format — not FHIR, C-CDA, or any external standard. The export is described as a \"manual one-time export\" that an organization initiates for one or more patients.\n\nThe page explicitly distinguishes this EHI export from the FHIR API (used for (g)(10) integrations) and directs developers interested in integration to the separate Developer Portal. This clear separation is a positive sign — Netsmart is not conflating (b)(10) with (g)(10).\n\n### Export Files (23 total)\n\nThe export produces 23 distinct files per patient, each as a separate JSON file:\n\n| # | File | Fields | Domain |\n|---|------|--------|--------|\n| 1 | **Demographics** | 29 | Patient demographics (name, DOB, SSN, race, ethnicity, language, gender identity, pronouns, etc.) |\n| 2 | **CCD** | — | C-CDA XML document with 19 clinical sections (allergies, meds, problems, labs, vitals, immunizations, procedures, care team, etc.) |\n| 3 | **FamilyHealthHistory** | 8 | Family member health conditions with SNOMED coding |\n| 4 | **HealthInsurance** | 15 | Insurance plans, coverage, policy numbers, eligibility |\n| 5 | **Referrals** | 36 | Admissions and referrals with source, status, care setting, discharge details, location history |\n| 6 | **ResponsibleParties** | 21 | Related parties with addresses, phone numbers, and relationships |\n| 7 | **CensusAdvanceDirectives** | 12 | Advance directives with type, dates, ordering physician |\n| 8 | **AssessmentandPlanOfTreatment** | 14 | Goals and interventions with form/chart status |\n| 9 | **Consents** | 9 | Consent forms with descriptions and captured values |\n| 10 | **Attachments** | — | Raw files (PDF, DOC, XLS, JPG, PNG, GIF, TIF, BMP, TXT, RTF, XML) |\n| 11 | **Documents** | 9 | Document metadata with base64-encoded document content |\n| 12 | **PatientNotes** | 27 | Clinical/administrative notes with categories, lock status, follow-up, addenda |\n| 13 | **Orders** | 37 | Physician orders (medications, advance directives) with dose, route, schedule, diagnoses |\n| 14 | **OrderAdministrations** | 41 | Medication administration records with physical monitors (vitals at administration) |\n| 15 | **Claims** | 29 | Claims/invoices with payer, charges, payments, adjustments, CBSA, certification periods |\n| 16 | **ClaimCharges** | 18 | Charge details with CPT/HCPCS, revenue codes, modifiers, amounts |\n| 17 | **ClaimChargeAdjustments** | 10 | Payment/adjustment transactions with type and batch |\n| 18 | **RegulatoryAssessment** | 14 | MDS, OASIS, and Hospice Item Set assessments with ASCII/XML submission strings |\n| 19 | **EventADTs** | 5 | ADT events (admit/discharge/transfer) with message type and timestamp |\n| 20 | **Appointments** | 10 | Scheduled/completed appointments with service and status |\n| 21 | **Eligibility** | 14 | Insurance eligibility verification requests and results |\n| 22 | **Authorization** | 20 | Insurance authorization details with quantities and time periods |\n| 23 | **NonRegulatoryAssessment** | 26 | Non-regulated assessments with question/answer pairs (e.g., custom clinical assessments) |\n\n### Documentation Detail\n\nEach export file is documented with:\n- **File-level description** of what the file contains\n- **Field-level definitions** with name, data type, and description\n- Data types include: String, Integer, Date, Time, Timestamp, Boolean, Number, Money, Decimal, Array, Base64 encoded binary, Date/Time\n- Descriptions are generally clear and actionable, explaining what each field represents and how it relates to the clinical workflow\n- The CCD file references USCDI v1 and the ONC 2015 Cures Update standard\n- Regulatory assessments include the raw ASCII/XML submission strings used for CMS reporting\n\n### Key Design Decisions\n\n- **Patient linkage**: `PatientID` is the primary cross-file join key, described as the MRN\n- **Admission linkage**: `AdmissionID` links referrals and order administrations to specific admissions\n- **Invoice linkage**: `InvoiceSys` joins Claims, ClaimCharges, and ClaimChargeAdjustments\n- **Nested structures**: NonRegulatoryAssessment and RegulatoryAssessment use arrays with dot-notation field names (e.g., `AssessmentDocumentID.HumanReadableValue`)\n- **Raw document export**: Both Attachments (raw files) and Documents (base64-encoded in JSON) are included\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\n**Well-covered domains:**\n\n- **Demographics**: Comprehensive — 29 fields covering name, DOB, SSN, race, ethnicity, language, gender identity, pronouns, military status, employment, education, death date/time. Strong coverage of USCDI demographic requirements.\n- **Clinical data via CCD**: The C-CDA document covers allergies, medications, problems, procedures, immunizations, labs, vitals, care team, encounters, goals, social history — the standard USCDI clinical summary. However, this is a structured summary, not raw clinical data.\n- **Orders and medication administration**: Detailed — 37 order fields and 41 administration fields including scheduling, physical monitors (vitals), follow-ups, and notes. Good eMAR representation.\n- **Billing/claims**: Strong — three linked files (Claims, ClaimCharges, ClaimChargeAdjustments) with 57 total fields covering invoices, CPT/HCPCS codes, revenue codes, modifiers, charges, payments, adjustments, authorizations, and payer details. This is genuinely comprehensive billing data, not just a summary.\n- **Assessments**: Two separate files for regulatory (MDS/OASIS/Hospice Item Sets with raw CMS submission data) and non-regulatory assessments (question/answer pairs). The regulatory assessment includes the full ASCII/XML submission string — essentially the complete assessment content.\n- **Insurance**: Covered across HealthInsurance (15 fields), Eligibility (14 fields), and Authorization (20 fields).\n- **Notes**: 27-field PatientNotes file with categories, alerts, locking, addenda, and follow-ups.\n- **Documents/attachments**: Both raw file attachments and document repository content with base64 encoding.\n- **Referrals/admissions**: 36-field Referrals file covering the full admission lifecycle from referral through discharge.\n- **Advance directives**: Dedicated file with 12 fields.\n- **Consents**: 9-field file for consent forms.\n- **Care plans**: AssessmentandPlanOfTreatment includes goals and interventions.\n\n**Potentially missing or underrepresented domains:**\n\n- **Vital signs as discrete data**: Vitals appear in the CCD (structured summary) and as physical monitors within OrderAdministrations, but there is no dedicated vitals file with time-series vital sign observations. For a post-acute care platform, discrete vital sign tracking is clinically important.\n- **Allergies as discrete data**: Only present within the CCD; no separate structured allergy file.\n- **Diagnoses/problem list as discrete data**: Only in the CCD. The Orders file has `Order_RelatedDiagnoses` but there's no standalone diagnosis file.\n- **Immunizations as discrete data**: Only within the CCD.\n- **Lab results as discrete data**: Only within the CCD.\n- **Wound care documentation**: For a post-acute/home health platform, wound care is a major clinical workflow (measurements, staging, photos). Not explicitly present beyond what may be captured in non-regulatory assessments or notes.\n- **ADL tracking**: Activities of daily living are core to SNF and senior living. May be captured in regulatory assessments (MDS includes ADL data in the XML string) but not as discrete data.\n- **Dietary/nutrition records**: Not present as a dedicated export.\n- **Therapy notes**: Physical, occupational, speech therapy documentation is not a distinct file (though may be in PatientNotes or NonRegulatoryAssessment).\n- **Electronic Visit Verification (EVV)**: myUnity has EVV via Mobile Caregiver+; EVV records are not explicitly in the export.\n- **Telehealth session records**: Not present.\n- **Scheduling/visit details**: Appointments file covers scheduled appointments, but the detailed visit documentation workflow data (visit notes, time in/out for home health visits) is not explicit beyond what's in PatientNotes.\n\n**Important nuance on CCD coverage**: Many \"missing\" clinical data domains (allergies, problems, meds, labs, vitals, immunizations, procedures) ARE exported — but within the CCD XML document, not as separate queryable JSON files. This means the data is present but in a standards-based summary format that may not capture every historical entry, custom field, or vendor-specific detail. The CCD is based on USCDI v1 / C-CDA R2.1, which has known limitations for data fidelity compared to the native EHR data model.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\n- **Primary format**: Vendor-native JSON files in a ZIP archive — a reasonable choice for (b)(10) since it captures the actual data model\n- **Secondary format**: C-CDA XML for the CCD file (standardized clinical summary)\n- **Attachments**: Raw files exported as-is (multiple file types supported)\n- **Documents**: Base64-encoded within JSON\n- **Regulatory assessments**: Include the actual CMS submission strings (ASCII/XML), which is excellent — these are the definitive regulatory records\n\nThe JSON format is proprietary but well-documented. Field names are descriptive. Data types are specified. Cross-file relationships are documented through shared IDs. A developer could implement an import of this data using only the PDF documentation.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\n**Strengths:**\n- Clear, consistent structure across all 23 files\n- Every field has a name, type, and description\n- File-level descriptions explain purpose\n- Glossary defines common cross-file fields (PatientSys, PatientID, Patient_DisplayName)\n- Explicit variability disclaimer acknowledging organization-specific differences\n- Clear separation from FHIR API documentation (no (b)(10)/(g)(10) confusion)\n\n**Weaknesses:**\n- No sample data or example export files provided\n- No value set documentation for coded fields (e.g., what are the possible values for `Order_Status`, `Patient_AdmissionStatus`, `Appointment_Status`?)\n- No explicit schema files (JSON Schema, OpenAPI) — only the PDF\n- No documentation of the ZIP structure (naming conventions, directory layout)\n- No versioning or change history beyond \"Last Updated: 08/15/2024\"\n- Relationship diagrams between files would help (e.g., how Claims → ClaimCharges → ClaimChargeAdjustments join)\n- The PDF format is not ideal for a data dictionary — a CSV, JSON Schema, or HTML table would be more machine-readable\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Granularity**: Field-level documentation with names, types, and descriptions — above average for EHI export documentation\n- **Value sets**: Not documented. Coded fields like status, type, and category fields lack enumerated possible values\n- **Relationships**: Implicitly documented through shared IDs (PatientID, InvoiceSys, Order_ID) but not formally diagrammed\n- **Cardinality**: Not explicitly documented. Arrays are mentioned (NonRegulatoryAssessment) but 1:N relationships are mostly implied\n- **Versioning**: Single version date (08/15/2024). No change log\n\n## Overall Assessment\n\nNetsmart's myUnity EHI export documentation is **above average** for the industry. Key positive findings:\n\n1. **Genuine (b)(10) export**: This is clearly a purpose-built EHI export, not repackaged FHIR API documentation. The JSON-in-ZIP format exports native data structures.\n2. **Broad data coverage**: 23 export files spanning demographics, clinical notes, orders, medication administration, billing (claims/charges/adjustments), assessments (both regulatory and non-regulatory), insurance, and documents/attachments.\n3. **Billing data included**: Three linked billing files with CPT codes, revenue codes, and payment transactions. Many vendors omit billing entirely.\n4. **Regulatory assessments preserved**: MDS, OASIS, and Hospice Item Sets are exported with their full CMS submission strings — the most complete representation possible.\n5. **Good field-level documentation**: 404 fields across 23 files, each with type and description.\n\nKey concerns:\n\n1. **CCD dependency for core clinical data**: Allergies, problems, medications, labs, vitals, and immunizations appear to be exported only within the CCD (a clinical summary), not as discrete vendor-native JSON. This means the richest clinical data may be limited to what USCDI v1 covers, while the vendor's native data model likely contains more detail (custom fields, historical entries, vendor-specific extensions).\n2. **No sample data**: Without example exports, it's hard to verify that the documentation matches reality.\n3. **Missing value sets**: Coded fields lack enumerated values, making import implementation harder.\n4. **Post-acute specialty gaps**: For a platform serving home health, hospice, SNF, and senior living, some domain-specific data may be underrepresented (wound care, ADLs, EVV, therapy-specific notes) — though these could be captured within the generic assessment and notes structures.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://www.ntst.com/lp/certifications/ehi-all-data-myunity\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no\n- Navigation complexity: one_click (from certifications hub to product-specific EHI page)\n- Anti-bot issues: none\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- None. The documentation was straightforward to find and download. The certifications page clearly organizes EHI documentation by product with dedicated pages per product line.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1186,"cache_read_input_tokens":101672,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1186},"output_tokens":1,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"db0d5107-7ffe-4c49-89d2-6ef77b08d733","uuid":"0300460e-e6cd-48b0-8459-a82d105c02bd"}

The CCD is based on USCDI v1 / C-CDA R2.1, which has known limitations for data fidelity compared to the native EHR data model.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\n- **Primary format**: Vendor-native JSON files in a ZIP archive — a reasonable choice for (b)(10) since it captures the actual data model\n- **Secondary format**: C-CDA XML for the CCD file (standardized clinical summary)\n- **Attachments**: Raw files exported as-is (multiple file types supported)\n- **Documents**: Base64-encoded within JSON\n- **Regulatory assessments**: Include the actual CMS submission strings (ASCII/XML), which is excellent — these are the definitive regulatory records\n\nThe JSON format is proprietary but well-documented. Field names are descriptive. Data types are specified. Cross-file relationships are documented through shared IDs. A developer could implement an import of this data using only the PDF documentation.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\n**Strengths:**\n- Clear, consistent structure across all 23 files\n- Every field has a name, type, and description\n- File-level descriptions explain purpose\n- Glossary defines common cross-file fields (PatientSys, PatientID, Patient_DisplayName)\n- Explicit variability disclaimer acknowledging organization-specific differences\n- Clear separation from FHIR API documentation (no (b)(10)/(g)(10) confusion)\n\n**Weaknesses:**\n- No sample data or example export files provided\n- No value set documentation for coded fields (e.g., what are the possible values for `Order_Status`, `Patient_AdmissionStatus`, `Appointment_Status`?)\n- No explicit schema files (JSON Schema, OpenAPI) — only the PDF\n- No documentation of the ZIP structure (naming conventions, directory layout)\n- No versioning or change history beyond \"Last Updated: 08/15/2024\"\n- Relationship diagrams between files would help (e.g., how Claims → ClaimCharges → ClaimChargeAdjustments join)\n- The PDF format is not ideal for a data dictionary — a CSV, JSON Schema, or HTML table would be more machine-readable\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Granularity**: Field-level documentation with names, types, and descriptions — above average for EHI export documentation\n- **Value sets**: Not documented. Coded fields like status, type, and category fields lack enumerated possible values\n- **Relationships**: Implicitly documented through shared IDs (PatientID, InvoiceSys, Order_ID) but not formally diagrammed\n- **Cardinality**: Not explicitly documented. Arrays are mentioned (NonRegulatoryAssessment) but 1:N relationships are mostly implied\n- **Versioning**: Single version date (08/15/2024). No change log\n\n## Overall Assessment\n\nNetsmart's myUnity EHI export documentation is **above average** for the industry. Key positive findings:\n\n1. **Genuine (b)(10) export**: This is clearly a purpose-built EHI export, not repackaged FHIR API documentation. The JSON-in-ZIP format exports native data structures.\n2. **Broad data coverage**: 23 export files spanning demographics, clinical notes, orders, medication administration, billing (claims/charges/adjustments), assessments (both regulatory and non-regulatory), insurance, and documents/attachments.\n3. **Billing data included**: Three linked billing files with CPT codes, revenue codes, and payment transactions. Many vendors omit billing entirely.\n4. **Regulatory assessments preserved**: MDS, OASIS, and Hospice Item Sets are exported with their full CMS submission strings — the most complete representation possible.\n5. **Good field-level documentation**: 404 fields across 23 files, each with type and description.\n\nKey concerns:\n\n1. **CCD dependency for core clinical data**: Allergies, problems, medications, labs, vitals, and immunizations appear to be exported only within the CCD (a clinical summary), not as discrete vendor-native JSON. This means the richest clinical data may be limited to what USCDI v1 covers, while the vendor's native data model likely contains more detail (custom fields, historical entries, vendor-specific extensions).\n2. **No sample data**: Without example exports, it's hard to verify that the documentation matches reality.\n3. **Missing value sets**: Coded fields lack enumerated values, making import implementation harder.\n4. **Post-acute specialty gaps**: For a platform serving home health, hospice, SNF, and senior living, some domain-specific data may be underrepresented (wound care, ADLs, EVV, therapy-specific notes) — though these could be captured within the generic assessment and notes structures.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://www.ntst.com/lp/certifications/ehi-all-data-myunity\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no\n- Navigation complexity: one_click (from certifications hub to product-specific EHI page)\n- Anti-bot issues: none\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- None. The documentation was straightforward to find and download.
